newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Helmut Kohl pledges EU will crackdown on crime.
newsitem.headline: Helmut Kohl pledges EU will crackdown on crime.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl promised the European Union's 300 million citizens on Wednesday that the bloc would crack down on drugs and crime.

"I do believe that the citizens of Europe expect us to show great determination in combating crime and ... particularly organised crime, the mafia and the drugs mafia in particular," Kohl told reporters on the first day of a visit to Ireland.

Kohl's words struck home in a country suffering what police say is a major drug crisis and a crime wave. Its foremost investigative reporter, Veronica Guerin, was shot dead by killers believed hired by a drug baron earlier this year.
Kohl was speaking after talks with Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, whose country holds the current EU presidency and which will host the first of two summits in Dublin this weekend.

Kohl said Saturday's informal Dublin summit would allow leaders to have a frank exchange on the progress of an Inter Governmental Conference (IGC) charged with recasting the bloc's founding treaties to streamline it for the 21st century.
They would "speak very frankly to each other in discussions aimed at reaching understandings to get the best results from the continuing Intergovernmental Conference on the future of the union".
"We will use the meeting as a preparation for more important work to be done at a more substantive formal council session near the end of this year," he said.
He told the Irish parliament that the enlargement of the EU to include former Soviet bloc states was "not only a historic but a moral obligation."
"It is also in all our interests, political, economic and cultural. Warsaw, Budapest and Prague are just as much an integral part of Europe as Berlin, Paris and Dublin," he said.
"Especially for us Germans, it is inconceivable that Poland's Western frontier should ultimately remain the European Union's eastern border," said Kohl.
Kohl arrived in Dublin on Wednesday for the first official bilateral visit by a German chancellor since 1979. He last visited Ireland in 1990 to attend an EU Dublin summit.

Bruton paid tribute to Kohl's vision for reuniting Germany and for putting forward the notion of enlarging the EU, that will bring the countries of the East "into closer democracy with the rest of Europe".
Bruton said the outcome of his exchanges with Kohl would "raise the sights and increase the ambitions" of Saturday's informal summit.
Thursday is the anniversary of Germany's reunification in 1990 and Kohl was to host a Unity Day reception in the Irish capital before leaving for home.
Kohl thanked Ireland for its unstinting and unequivocable support when Germany was trying to unite East and West. He said other neighbouring countries were not so encouraging.
"I have always been supported by Ireland and I shall not forget this," Kohl said.
He said Europe was on the road to building one European home and what was important was to make all voices heard whether they were from large or small countries.
"Let all these voices be heard and that should not be depending on the size of the country. It is quality not quantity that counts," he said.
